criteria.always_lazy: Every request keeps its body unread until the handler acts. The first body access consumes the wire stream: buffered operations drain it into memory up to the configured cap, opening a reader hands the live stream over. A body larger than the cap surfaces as a domain failure inside the handler, and the fixed 413 exists only when handler code maps that failure to it.
criteria.eager_only: Every request keeps the current drain-first ingress: the adapter buffers the whole body up to the cap before dispatch, oversize yields a fixed 413 without invoking the handler, and streaming readers always serve from those buffered bytes. True wire-incremental reads are out of scope and the memory bound is documented.
criteria.route_marked: Routes stay buffered unless marked: unmarked routes keep drain-first ingress with the fixed pre-dispatch 413, while routes wrapped in a streaming marker skip the pre-read and hand the handler a live body the handler reads once through a stream reader. One catalogue marker carries the choice.

body_mode.instructions: How should the server choose between buffered and incremental request bodies?

criteria.buffered_repeatable: Buffered body, JSON, form and multipart reads stay repeatable from cached bytes. Opening a body reader is one-shot per request; once a live reader is open, buffered reads fail with body consumed. Opening a reader after buffered reads serves the cached bytes from memory.
criteria.mode_exclusive: The first body access fixes the request in one mode: any buffered operation locks buffered mode, opening a reader locks live mode, and crossing modes afterwards fails. Buffered reads repeat inside buffered mode; the live reader is one-shot.
criteria.single_shot: Every body access consumes exactly once: any second body read of any kind, including calling the buffered body operation twice, fails. Handlers bind the body a single time and reuse the bound value.

consumption.instructions: Which consumption rules should govern mixed buffered and streaming body reads?

criteria.callback_fold: One response operation takes status, headers and a producer callback and drives chunk production internally, closing and erroring the wire stream itself. Handlers never hold a writer handle.
criteria.reader_pipe: A response operation takes status, headers and an existing stream reader and pipes that reader as the response body. Production happens wherever the reader came from, not in the responding handler.
criteria.writer_pair: A response operation returns a pending response and a separate operation vends its stream writer exactly once. The handler writes chunks with the shared write operation, closes the writer, and returns the pending response.

response_stream.instructions: How should handlers produce streaming response bodies?

criteria.arg_send: One send operation takes the writer plus positional data, event, id and retry arguments with empty-for-absent conventions. No event record type exists.
criteria.raw_stream: No event operation exists. Handlers format Server-Sent Event text themselves through the shared byte writer and own framing correctness.
criteria.record_send: A fixed event record carries data, event, id and retry fields with empty-for-absent conventions. A send operation validates framing and rejects line injection; a comment operation covers heartbeat lines.

sse_shape.instructions: What surface should Server-Sent Event production use?

state: Can HTTP serves requests through Bun.serve on pinned Bun 1.4.2. Today the adapter drains each request body fully, bounded by the server body cap, before dispatch; a larger body yields a fixed 413 and the handler never runs, and buffered body, JSON and form reads repeat from cached bytes. Both behaviors are pinned by tests. B1-05 pull streams exist: opaque byte readers and writers with read_many bounded by a per-chunk cap, write_some with accepted counts, close and cancel, no prefetch queue, and no cumulative byte cap. B1-06 requires incremental request bodies through read_many with per-chunk caps, reporting chunk order, genuine connection termination, framing violations and consumption violations; a second read of a consumed body must fail; slow clients must cap response buffering through backpressure; routes must cover PUT, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS and HEAD; TLS and Server-Sent Events are required. Pinned probes observed: request.body is a live stream and leaving it unread never blocks the response; cancelling it then responding works; client disconnect rejects a pending server read with AbortError and aborts the request signal; Bun strips HEAD bodies natively; header entries already split Set-Cookie both directions; a mid-stream response error reaches the client as a silently truncated 200. Fixed constraints: catalogue additions only with no new grammar, the eager-413 and repeatable-read pins hold unless the decision explicitly moves them, owner lifecycle stays open to closing to closed with request-scoped handles, and acceptance evidence outranks this advice.
